subject: Clarify service-use boundary clauses and feedback/training language
messages:
From: Quantix Legal <contracts@quantix.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@quantix.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quantix – redlines on MSA & Order Form (IP + training)

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Attached are our redlines to the MSA and the Order Form — see pages 4-6 (output use) and 11 (training/feedback). Our legal team wants explicit assurance that: 

- Quantix retains exclusive ownership of customer-provided prompts and edited outputs used directly as product content;
- Redwood will not use customer data or outputs to retrain or fine-tune models without separate consent;
- There is a limited feedback license for service improvements but only on aggregated, de-identified signal.

We flagged alternative language inline for an option that permits anonymized telemetry for ops and perf work. Please confirm whether the fallback language in the PDF is acceptable or if Redwood proposes different guardrails.

Attachments: Quantix_Redlines_20260621.pdf (pdf, 6 pages)

Thanks,
Dana Park
Head of Legal — Quantix AI
Dana Park | Quantix AI

Subject: Re: Quantix – redlines on MSA & Order Form (IP + training)

Thanks Dana — got the redlines and the notes. Looping in Laura (legal) and Marissa (product/ops) to confirm practical constraints. Quick summary of what we'll validate internally:

1) Output ownership carveouts vs. our standard customer output position — can we hold to a non-exclusive license for outputs used to serve the customer vs. an assignment?
2) Training prohibition scope — clarify whether "use for model updates" includes offline evals and aggregated prompts; we generally allow telemetry for safety/quality unless customer opts out.
3) Feedback license wording — we have a standard limited feedback license; we'll propose more explicit de-identification and retention windows.

Next steps: Laura will propose redline language we can attach to the MSA; Marissa will confirm operational feasibility (telemetry pipelines, retention periods); I'll draft a short mutual action plan for procurement so Quantix can accept quickly if the clauses land.

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Quantix Legal <contracts@quantix.ai>, Dana Park <dana.park@quantix.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-21T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Quantix – redlines on MSA & Order Form (IP + training)

Karthik / Dana — reviewed the PDF. High-level position below plus proposed edits attached (proposed-clause-draft.docx). I tried to balance Quantix's request for strong ownership protections with our operational need to improve service.

Proposed positions (summary):
- Output ownership: Redwood will grant Quantix a perpetual, worldwide right to use customer-provided content and output for Quantix's productization of that content (i.e., product embeds/derivative works) only if Quantix explicitly requests assignment; absent that request, Redwood retains a non-exclusive license to operate and deliver the service to the account.

- Training / model updates: Redwood will not use customer-provided prompts, proprietary data, or generated outputs to train, fine-tune, or update base model weights that are used to serve other customers unless Quantix gives written opt-in consent. We will, however, be permitted to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for safety and performance monitoring subject to a 90-day retention window and deletion on request.

- Feedback license: Offer a limited feedback license that permits use of customer feedback for internal service improvement and bug fixes, with controls: 1) de-identification, 2) retention period (90 days), 3) option for account-level opt-out in Order Form.

Operational notes for Marissa: please confirm the telemetry pipeline can produce aggregated, de-identified artifacts and that we can support an account-level opt-out flag with a 90-day retention. If we can't meet 90 days, propose alternative (e.g., 30 or 120).

Attachments: proposed-clause-draft.docx (docx)

If Quantix likes this language, Karthik — I suggest we prepare a short amendment to the Order Form that spells out the opt-in checkbox and the retention shortcode; then procurement can accept and we can attach as Schedule X.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Dana Park <dana.park@quantix.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@quantix.ai>, contracts@quantix.ai
Date: 2026-06-22T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Quantix – redlines on MSA & Order Form (IP + training)

Laura / Karthik — thanks for the quick review and the proposed wording. Quantix can accept the approach with one minor change: we want the retention window for telemetry used for product improvements limited to 60 days rather than 90. That better aligns with our internal data lifecycle.

If Redwood is ok with 60 days, we can sign the Order Form amendment and move forward with procurement. Please send the amendment as a DocuSign link and include the HubSpot deal ID so our procurement team can reference the record.

Next steps for Redwood:
- Update proposed-clause-draft.docx to reflect 60-day telemetry retention and regenerate redline PDF.
- Send DocuSign amendment to contracts@quantix.ai and include HubSpot link (we'll confirm PO once signed).

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9314
